blocks.label: What it is
blocks.text: A milestone is a group of tasks for one goal, where at least one task waits for another. You approve its plan before any of its tasks builds.

blocks.label: Why it exists
blocks.text: Some requests are too big for one pull request. A milestone keeps their tasks together and runs one pilot task first. The other tasks start only after the pilot merges, so a wrong idea costs one task, not eight.

blocks.label: A real example
blocks.text: Milestone 5, Sage feel, has 8 tasks. The pilot is the presentation skill; the 7 playbooks wait for it. You approved its plan on 10 Nov. It is done when each task that is not stopped is done.

blocks.title: How it works: a milestone in its release
blocks.key: Key: each box names its level. The arrow means “waits for”. A release and a milestone are both optional.
lines: │ │ │ Runs first, from start to merge    │ │ │
│ │ Done when each task that is not        │ │
│ │ Each one pull request or one study     │ │

blocks.label: Like, and where the likeness stops
blocks.text: It is like a milestone in a project plan: one goal and the work for it. But a sage milestone has no date. It ends when its tasks are done, not on a day.

blocks.label: What it is not
blocks.text: It is not a release: a release is a version that you ship, such as 1.0, and it holds milestones and single tasks. It is not a task: a task is one pull request or one study.

items: pilot: the one task of a milestone that runs from start to merge first.
release: a version that you ship. Optional.
Old word: program. You retired it on 11 Nov; now it means only a computer program.
